  • Fabric that becomes softer with each wash
  • Natural breathability enhanced through traditional treatment
  • Chemical-free comfort against your skin

4. Geographical Indication Protected Craft

🧵 The Sacred Art of Sanganeri Block Printing Process

Traditional 5-Stage Creation Process Your Dress Undergoes

Stage 1: Hari Sarana (Purification) Before printing, dirt and dust are washed from cloth so prints are vibrant. Fabric is submerged in bleach and water solution, then washed with boiling water.

Stage 2: Marking (Preparation) Cloth is marked with chalk and scale to help with printing process, so artisan can see where blocks should be placed.

Stage 3: Chapaai (The Sacred Printing) Printing process uses wooden or metal blocks. Cloth is printed left to right, with number of blocks depending on colors used.

Stage 4: Sukhaai (Natural Drying) Natural drying process ensures color gets secured on cloth through traditional sun-drying methods.

Stage 5: Dhulaai (Purification Wash) Final washing and finishing that gives the fabric its characteristic soft feel and lasting color vibrancy.
